title: Tomato and Egg Scramble

items: ¼ tsp kosher salt, plus a pinch for the tomatoes
1 scallion, thinly sliced, white and green parts kept separate
2 cups cooked white rice, warm, or 2 slices toast

steps: Beat the eggs with ¼ tsp salt in a small bowl until no streaks of white remain.
Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Pour in the eggs, let them sit 10 sec, then push them slowly from the edges to the center with a spatula.
When the eggs are mostly set but still a little wet and glossy, 1–2 min, slide them onto a plate. They finish cooking later.
Add the remaining 1 Tbsp oil and the scallion whites to the pan over medium heat and stir 30 sec. Add the tomatoes, sugar, a pinch of salt and 2 Tbsp water.
Cook 3–5 min, stirring and pressing some tomatoes with the spatula, until they burst and turn saucy.
Return the eggs and fold gently 30–60 sec, until no runny egg remains and the eggs are coated in the tomato sauce.
Top with the scallion greens. Serve over rice or with toast.
tips: Pull the eggs early. They keep cooking in the hot tomatoes, and dry, rubbery eggs are the most common mistake here.
Only have regular tomatoes? Cut 2 into wedges and cook them 4–5 min.
Add 1 tsp soy sauce to the tomatoes for a more savory sauce.
storage: Best eaten right away. Leftovers keep 1 day in the fridge. Reheat in the microwave in 20-sec bursts, just until warm.
